title: Results diary
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Changes of materials and animals including humans
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 22 (Results diary (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 22: Oxidation: rusting and browning. To understand that rusting and browning are irreversible changes caused by oxygen

questions.q: Why does an iron gate get painted?
questions.a: Paint keeps water and oxygen away, so it does not rust
questions.model: What does rust need? Water and oxygen. Paint covers the iron, so neither can reach it. So no rust.

questions.a: No, it makes a new material

questions.q: Why does lemon juice stop apple browning?
questions.a: It slows the reaction with oxygen

questions.q: Set up the four nail jars and three apple slices (no coating, lemon juice, cling film). Record day 1 and predictions.
questions.a: Predictions: salt water nail rusts fastest, dry nail does not; plain apple browns, lemon and cling film slices brown less
questions.model: Teacher sets up jar 1 on camera and writes: 'Jar 1, tap water: I predict rust in 3 days.'

questions.q: Which jar is the control? Why?
questions.a: Jar 1 (tap water): ordinary conditions to compare the others with

questions.q: How do people stop bicycles rusting? Give two ways.
questions.a: Oil the chain, paint the frame, keep it dry or indoors

questions.q: Big question: why does a cut apple brown but not one in its skin?
questions.a: The cut surface reacts with oxygen; the skin keeps the oxygen out.
